title: Ethical Robustness Verification for BCI Systems: Bridging Safety and Human Rights
summary: This paper introduces a framework for verifying BCI systems against adversarial threats while ensuring compliance with proposed neuro-rights (e.g., cognitive liberty, mental privacy). It formalizes robustness requirements as quadratic constraints and integrates them into a semidefinite programming (SDP) verification pipeline.
gap: Current robustness verification methods (e.g., SDP-based) do not account for ethical considerations unique to BCIs, such as mental privacy or autonomy. Existing neuro-rights frameworks lack actionable technical implementations.
approach: Extend SDP-based robustness verification to include constraints derived from neuro-rights principles (e.g., bounded input perturbations for privacy). Develop a certification pipeline that jointly optimizes accuracy, robustness, and ethical compliance.
evaluation: Test the framework on EEGNet and other BCI models using datasets with sensitive information (e.g., error-related negativity). Measure certification rates, classification accuracy, and perturbation bounds under ethical constraints.
